newsitem.title: USA: Virgin Islands approves $27 million wages payment.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Islands approves $27 million wages payment.

text.p: Some U.S. Virgin Islands government officials Thursday questioned the effect of the Senate's vote Wednesday to approve $27 million for partial payment to more than 13,000 government employees owed retroactive wages.

The government said the approval could mean a possibility of "payless paydays," unless the territory can arrange a loan to meet the $13 million biweekly payroll or that 1994 and 1995 income tax refunds would be put on hold indefinitely.
It might also mean a delay in paying vendors for goods and services already delivered to the government or other financial austerity measures like hiring freezes and cuts in travel.
Of the money approved by the Senate, $15 million came from pre-payment of property taxes by Hess Oil Virgin Islands Corp.
